title: Build a tiny fixed thread pool

task.text: Implement `MiniPool`: a fixed set of reusable workers fed by a bounded queue.

items: `MiniPool(int threads, int capacity)` starts `threads` workers at once. Tasks wait in a queue of `capacity`.
`execute(Runnable)` queues a task, waiting while the queue is full. After `shutdown()` has begun it throws `RejectedExecutionException`.
A task that throws must not kill its worker.
`shutdown()` lets every queued task finish, then returns once all workers have exited.
Build it yourself: no `Executors`, no `ThreadPoolExecutor`, and no thread per task.

checks.title: At most N tasks run at once
A full queue makes execute wait
A failing task does not kill a worker
Tasks wait in a bounded BlockingQueue
The pool builds its own workers

hints.text: A pool is a producer-consumer pair inside one object: `execute` is the producer, and each worker loops taking a task and running it. The queue gives you both the waiting and the bound.

Create the workers in the constructor, each running a `take()` loop on an `ArrayBlockingQueue<Runnable>`. For shutdown, set a flag so `execute` rejects, then queue one stop marker per worker and join them. Catch `RuntimeException` around each task.
